newsitem.title: USA: Rap star Shakur critically wounded in Las Vegas.
newsitem.headline: Rap star Shakur critically wounded in Las Vegas.

text.p: Rap music star Tupac Shakur was listed in critical condition on Sunday after he was shot three times in the chest when the car he was riding in was ambushed and riddled with gunfire, authorities said.
Shakur, a 25-year-old singer-actor with a history of violence and trouble with the law, underwent emergency surgery after the Saturday night attack near the famed Las Vegas Strip.
It was the second time in less than two years that Shakur has been shot, and a hospital source said he had a "fairly good" chance of surviving his latest wounds.
Marion "Suge" Knight, 31, co-founder of the controversial music label Death Row Records, was driving the car and suffered a minor gunshot wound to the head, Las Vegas police said.
Knight, who produces the work of Shakur and other top rap stars, was treated and released on Sunday.

The attack occurred while Shakur, one of the most notorious performers of hardcore "Gangsta" rap, was headed for a nightclub with friends in a convoy of 10 cars after watching the Mike Tyson-Bruce Seldon heavyweight boxing title fight.

A white Cadillac with four people inside pulled up next to Shakur's black BMW and one of them opened fire, riddling the car with 12 or 13 bullets, police said. Dozens of stunned witnesses looked on in horror, according to broadcast reports.
Shakur, in the passenger seat, was hit three times in the chest and rushed to the hospital, officials said. The Cadillac sped away, and the suspects were still being sought, police said.
Investigators said the shooting was an apparent ambush but that the motive was not known.
Shakur is no stranger to trouble. He has spent much of the last 2-1/2 years in court, prison or hospital.
In November 1994, he was shot five times while being robbed of $40,000 in jewels in the lobby of a Manhattan recording studio.

In February 1995, Shakur was sentenced to prison for involvement in a sexual attack on a 21-year-old woman in a New York hotel room. He spent eight months behind bars until winning his release pending his appeal.
Shakur was convicted in 1994 of attacking a music video producer in Hollywood.
Last April in Los Angeles, Shakur was ordered to serve 120 days in jail for probation violations and for failing to complete his community service. He was allowed to remain free pending his appeal.

Following the title fight on Saturday night, Shakur was a passenger in a convoy that had formed near the casino district. When gunfire broke out, several of the vehicles raced away. The Cadillac chased Shakur's car, pulled up alongside it and riddled it with gunfire, police said.
Shakur was taken to University Medical Centre where he remained in intensive care after surgery, said hospital spokesman Dale Pugh.

Shakur is best known for raw lyrics laced with violence, sex and profanity describing life in the black ghetto. His latest album, "All Eyez on Me," released this year, celebrates his own outlaw image and has sold several million copies.
He appeared opposite pop star Janet Jackson in the 1993 movie "Poetic Justice" and was working on another film, "Gridlock."
